subject: Private deployment pricing sensitivity analysis and packaging options
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@medsight.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing sensitivity — private deploy options

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profile. Before we proceed to procurement, our CFO asked for a short sensitivity run comparing three commercial constructs for a private VPC deployment:

1) Flat platform fee + per-node operator licenses (lower capex, higher opex)
2) Annual reserved capacity (committed nodes) with amortized platform fee
3) Pure consumption (metered per-token but with higher support uplift)

Can you send a spreadsheet with assumed entry SKUs, examples of the first-year cost under medium (50k reqs/day) and high (200k reqs/day) workloads, and any discounts you would consider for a 24-month commitment? Also: we need a short SOC2 summary for our security team.

Would like this by EOD Monday if possible — procurement is trying to close Q2.

Best,
Alicia
Procurement Lead, MediSight

Attachments: none

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@medsight.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity — private deploy options

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear ask and for taking the time yesterday.

Quick summary: we can model the three constructs you listed. I attached a compact spreadsheet (MediSight_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx) with line items and three scenarios: Starter Pilot (2 operator seats, 4 nodes equivalent), Scale Reserved (10 committed nodes, amortized platform fee), and Metered Surge (no commit, per-token metered + 20% support uplift). Each scenario has cost rows for ~50k reqs/day and ~200k reqs/day; see columns labeled FY1_MEDIUM and FY1_HIGH.

Discounts: for a 24-month commitment we typically offer: 10% off platform fee for pilot->commit conversion, and a further tiered rebate on reserved nodes (5% at 10 nodes, 12% at 25 nodes). We can consider an introductory implementation credit to offset the first-month invoices for pilots.

SOC2: attached SOC2_Summary.pdf — it’s a two-page highlight for review (controls we commonly surface for private deployments). If your security team needs the full report we’ll route that via our compliance portal and an NDA.

Next steps: if you can confirm which of the three constructs procurement prefers to prioritize, we’ll produce a short SOW and a redlineable pilot SOW (pilot-sow-draft.docx).

Deliverables attached: MediSight_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx; SOC2_Summary.pdf; pilot-sow-draft.docx

Thanks — I’ll follow up internally on detailed support-band costing and flag any SRE on-call options that change the unit economics.

— Neha
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0112

Attachments: MediSight_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx, SOC2_Summary.pdf, pilot-sow-draft.docx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-14T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: need support tier / oncall inputs for MediSight scenarios

Marissa, Diego — forwarding Alicia’s procurement ask and the spreadsheet I attached to her. Two quick items I need today:

- Marissa: can you validate the support tiers in the spreadsheet? The sheet assumes three tiers (Standard: 9x5 email; Premier: 24x7 phone + 2h P1 response; Enterprise: 24x7 + SRE retainer). I put hourly oncall uplift as +15% for Premier, +30% for Enterprise; please confirm if these uplift multipliers are sane for a private VPC with 10 committed nodes.

- Diego: technical note re operator seats: Alicia asked about operator-license vs per-node. For the pilot we proposed 2 operator seats and 4 nodes equivalent. If we move to reserved nodes, the license curve changes; can you sanity-check the node-to-operator ratio and any hidden infra-cost multipliers (e.g., airgap packaging or extra runbook hours) that should go into the SOW?

Alicia wants the spreadsheet and SOC2 summary by EOD Monday; procurement is pushing Q2 close. If either of you think a different commercial construct (e.g., staggered commit) would materially change the pricing, call it out — I want a short note I can include in the reply.

Thanks — Neha

On 2025-06-14 08:12 Alicia Ramos wrote:
> Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profile. Before we proceed to procurement, our CFO asked for a short sensitivity run comparing three commercial constructs for a private VPC deployment:
> ...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-14T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: need support tier / oncall inputs for MediSight scenarios

Quick answers — ran numbers off the sheet:

- Support uplifts: 15% (Premier) and 30% (Enterprise) are fine as ballpark multipliers for FY1. For a 24-mo commit we can compress to 10% and 20% respectively, given predictable ARR.

- Hidden costs / runbook time: for air-gapped or on-prem packaging add a one-time implementation surcharge (~$18k) and plan for ~40 consulting hours for runbook/setup (we price at $250/hr in the pilot SOW template). I added these as separate lines in the attached spreadsheet (column NOTES_RUNBOOK).

- Operator-seat vs node: Diego — if you confirm the node-equivalence we can model an operator seat cap of 1 seat per 5 nodes for baseline; for high-availability customers we often recommend 1:3. For MediSight’s scale (10 nodes committed in the Scale scenario) 2 operator seats is conservative; 3 seats is safer if they want 24x7 on-call rotation.

Recommendation: present them the three scenarios but prominently call out a hybrid: reserve a modest anchor (5 nodes) + metered burst. That keeps capex predictable while preserving elasticity; commercial team can offer a 7.5% platform fee discount for a 24-mo anchored commit plus a one-time implementation credit (up to $15k) to close pilot-to-commit.

— Marissa
Director, Commercial Finance

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@medsight.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medsight.com>
Date: 2025-06-16T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity — private deploy options

Neha — thanks, the spreadsheet looks helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement/security: 

1) Procurement prefers the hybrid anchor + metered burst you recommended. Can you convert that into a short term-sheet showing: anchor size (5 nodes), committed price, burst per-token rate, and the 24-mo discount you proposed (7.5% platform fee discount + $15k implementation credit)?

2) Security wants the SOC2 full report; they said the summary is a good start but will need the report and an evidence list. Will you route the standard SOC2 NDA flow?

3) For internal finance we need to see a sample invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and an example pilot invoicing schedule that shows the implementation credit applied.

If you can send the term-sheet and invoice example by EOD Tuesday, we can slot this for an internal approval on Wednesday.

Best,
Alicia

Attachments: none

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@medsight.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity — private deploy options (term-sheet + next steps)

Alicia — thanks, great direction. Attaching a short commercial term-sheet and a sample invoice cadence (see MediSight_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx, tab TERM-SHEET and tab INVOICE_EXAMPLES). Quick notes:

- Anchor: 5 committed nodes, amortized platform fee at list less 7.5% discount for 24-month commitment. Burst: metered per-token with a stepped rate after 100M tokens/month. Implementation credit: $15,000 applied to the pilot invoice as a negative line item.

- Billing cadence: default monthly invoices with a net-30 for pilot customers; we can do quarterly invoicing with 2% surcharge if MediSight prefers less frequent invoices tied to internal controls.

- SOC2: we’ll route the full report via our compliance portal. I’ll send the portal link and NDA instructions to you in a separate note (security+legal require the portal handshake).

Next steps: if you sign off we’ll (1) circulate a one-page term-sheet for countersign, (2) send a pilot SOW redlineable doc, and (3) create a tight delivery plan for the runbook/setup window.

If procurement wants, I can also schedule a 30-minute call with our finance lead (Marissa) and Diego for the runbook details.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

— Neha
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MediSight_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx, SOC2_Summary.pdf, pilot-sow-draft.docx
